name: Encompass Health Corporation
moat_justification: Genuine scale, CON and referral-network advantages in a supply-constrained niche, but CMS sets the price, labor is ~52% of revenue, and measured ROIC has historically sat around the cost of capital — scale converts into volume, not wide-moat economics.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 6.7x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
one_liner: Durable IRF leader, moat 5/10 — good business, impossible price: weighted IRR 6.5% and IV@15% $38.90 vs $127.87; it only clears the 15% hurdle below ~$39.
moat_for: Largest US IRF operator (~22% of Medicare IRF discharges, 173 hospitals) — scale in recruiting, purchasing, protocols, payor contracting
Certificate-of-need regimes cap competing supply; national IRF bed supply flat for a decade vs aging Medicare population
66 joint ventures with acute-care systems hard-wire the referral pipeline
Clinical outcomes above industry averages (Q2 2026 discharge-to-community 84.7%) reinforce referral preference
moat_against: No real pricing power — CMS sets Medicare rates by annual rule (~+2.3% est. FY2027); managed care follows
ROIC proxy only 8.7–11.3% across 2016–2022 — around the cost of capital; capital-intensive model
Labor ~52% of revenue with guided wage inflation 3.5–4% for 2026, at or above the pricing update
Payer concentration and denial risk: Medicare RCD reviews, MA utilization management, TEAM episodic model
Growth consumes the cash — TTM capex $799.1M against TTM OCF $1,212.5M
